# glinet_firewall_port_forward_order (Resource)

Manages the order of the port forwards of the firewall, which the web UI of firmware 4.8.3 shows as their priority. The router has one order, so use one instance of this resource. The port forwards in `port_forwards` go first, in that order. The other port forwards go after them, in their order on the router. The provider sends the router IDs of all port forwards in the new order with `order_port_forward`, as the web UI does, and sends no write when the order on the router is already correct. Create and update fail when the router has no port forward with an identity of `port_forwards`. After the write, the provider reads the port forwards again and fails when their order is not the configured order. Terraform plans an update when the first port forwards on the router are not those of `port_forwards` in that order. Use the attributes of `glinet_firewall_port_forward` resources in `port_forwards`, so that Terraform creates the port forwards first. Firmware 4.7.0 does not have `order_port_forward`. The write was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. How the order applies to the traffic is not known. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_firewall_port_forward_order" "this" {
  port_forwards = [
    {
      external_zone = glinet_firewall_port_forward.game.external_zone
      protocol      = glinet_firewall_port_forward.game.protocol
      external_port = glinet_firewall_port_forward.game.external_port
    },
    {
      external_zone = glinet_firewall_port_forward.web.external_zone
      protocol      = glinet_firewall_port_forward.web.protocol
      external_port = glinet_firewall_port_forward.web.external_port
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `port_forwards` (Attributes List) The port forwards that go first, in that order. The external zone, the protocol and the external port identify a port forward, as in `glinet_firewall_port_forward`. When the router has more than one port forward with an identity, the first one moves and the others stay with the port forwards that are not in the list. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--port_forwards))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `firewall_port_forward_order`.

<a id="nestedatt--port_forwards"></a>
### Nested Schema for `port_forwards`

Required:

- `external_port` (String) External port, from 1 to 65535, or a range of ports such as `8000-8010` (`src_dport` in the router API).
- `external_zone` (String) Firewall zone that the traffic comes from, for example `wan` (`src` in the router API).
- `protocol` (String) Protocol: `tcp`, `udp` or `tcp udp` (`proto` in the router API).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "firewall_port_forward_order". The import reads all port forwards of the router in their order.
terraform import glinet_firewall_port_forward_order.this firewall_port_forward_order
```
